Constantly interrupted students when they answered questions she asked the class. Has strict/odd grading requirements and doesn't give a rubric; just expects students will somehow read her mind. Least favorite class I have taken in my academic career thus far
Did not know how to teach but there were two tests the whole year and you could BS the assignments.

You are also graded on very little in this class: a case study paper, 2 quizzes, and a large group project

analysis.name: Ivan Rupnik
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ivan, as a professor, is a very understanding and easy-to-talk-to person. The course ARCH 1110 is inherently challenging to teach and only really makes sense if you are an architecture major. The course covered so many things in such a short time, and for each project, you learn something new thats completely different from the week before.

Should not be considered a professor because he legit doesn't teach. Every single class, he goes through a 100 pg slideshow, critiques everyone's mistakes on drawings, then has the poor TAs teaching everything else. When we were struggling with the software, ESPECIALLY Rhino, he would get irritated and commanded TAs to scramble around. Terrible.

Class goes like this: Ivan critiques work from the previous assignment, then he has the TAs teach how to do the next assignment. If you're good with technology, time management, and willing to put in the time this class will be a breeze. If you're stuck, it's better to look up a youtube video or ask a classmate than waiting for office hours.

Ivan is arguably the worst person you could pick to teach this course. All of the learning and almost all the grading was facilitated by TAs, since he doesn't understand half the software that he teaches. Expect homework to take at least 5 hours a week, and you will have to learn most of the techniques yourself.

analysis.name: Hanai Sadaka
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 122 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Sadaka is without a doubt one of the most frustrating professors I've had at Northeastern. He has a smug attitude that I can't get over and an incredibly harsh grading policy.  Any arithmetic errors, regardless of whether or not you understand the concepts, can drop you a whole letter grade on quizzes. Should've dropped his class when I could!

Honestly I just don't like him and everything he does annoys me -- he has the most infuriating way of teaching. Every concept more difficult than it needs to be; if you miss 3 classes he drops a letter grades; he never directly answers student's questions, and alternates between whispering and shouting during the lecture. Also, super smug.

Hanai, Hanai, Hanai. Students let me tell you something. If you want a teacher that explains EVERYTHING there is to explain. Questions? He won't go forward on the content if 1 student does not understand the topic.  If you want a teacher that helps you to learn, to know everything and to prepare for the final exam, take him. BEST TEACHER IN NEU.

Do not take this teacher. They often rant and yell at the class, creating a hostile environment. Their tests are needlessly difficult, and they have made students cry. Once, they even threatened to drop a student for being two minutes late when class hadn't started yet. They fail to cover relevant material, and their office hours are non-existant

Hany bullies students and creates an environment that is unconducive to learning. Syllabus says attendance isn't mandatory, threatens to fail students who don't come to class. Acts annoyed and inconvenienced with students' presence. Questions are entirely discouraged. Made multiple students cry. The man is smart and knows what he's talking about.

analysis.name: Jennifer Ingemi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ingemi is a great professor, even if her lectures can be a bit dry at times. Tests are open note and not too bad, and she will go over everything in-depth at office hours. Easy points from discussion boards and extra credit at the end of the semester. Very manageable class if you pay attention, and lectures are recorded in case you don't.

Dr. Ingemi is a great professor who's really passionate about the course material. While a lot of the content is dense, she does a great job at explaining important concepts and is always open to answering questions. Also, quizzes and exams were both take home, but very application based and therefore required a lot of thinking and problem solving.

Professor Ingemi is a great professor. Class is pretty easy to do well in, exams are online and there are lots of extra credit opportunities. She obviously cares a lot about her students and is very open to accommodations when needed. Makes jokes in lectures and is generally very chill. Attendance is based on pollev and she drops 2 classes worth.

Dr. Ingemi is super nice and very knowledgeable. I would recommend her for any course neuroscience/biology related. Her lectures are SUPER dense but she records them. She does Poll Everywhere in class so you have to attend lectures. Her tests are online but she makes them really tricky. There's a lot of content in this class but she's great

Very nice woman, but her teaching style does not work for me (and probably many others). Lectures are dense, and she talks extremely slowly to the point where it's impossible to stay engaged. Very hard to take notes and slides were unhelpful. However, the exams are all online, so everyone does very well.

analysis.name: Zhengzhong Jin
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Tests are fair and the grading was very fair in my experience. Lectures are dry but Prof Jin was a nice guy and would take all the time you need to understand things. I think this was his second semester teaching and from what I heard previously he really has gotten his stuff together and is great now. A lot of time on HW though. Would take again!

If you attend lectures regularly and ask for help on homework questions, you will do well in Professor Jin's class. He is friendly and always willing to answer questions on Piazza or in person. Tests can be challenging, but final letter grades may be curved to compensate for that. Participation can also boost your grade. Overall, great professor!

This class in my opinion was amazing... Professor Jin is by far one of the best professors I've had - his passion with respect to theory makes learning enjoyable. I would recommend that if you do not enjoy proofs as much, potentially stay away from this class but overall Professor Jin makes it manageable and bearable. 10/10 if I could
The esteemed gentleman in question endeavours to take meticulous care that the entirety of one's comprehension be satisfactorily addressed.
I got cooked in both midterms but he is still the goat

Additionally, his lectures are poorly designed, covered entire full stack dev in just 2 lectures!

probably the worst class I have taken at northeastern. he packs assignments and exams to the absolute maximum and he was confused when the class average was a D- on the midterm and refusing to curve it. assignments take a very long time because he wants everyone to know web dev, and is not even teaching 5500, he randomly started teaching 5610.

Worst course.Overwhelming workload with project-like assignments, exams, class activities, & final project. Instructor reads from slides without ensuring student understanding. Significant portion of grades lies on last week's performance, with 25% for project & 35% for exam. If you don't perform well in final week, grades will significantly drop.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CS5500. The whole class is doing MERN stack web development, using JavaScript the whole time. Yes, you can learn a lot - by yourself! So many lecture notes and theories, none of them help you do the project - which is the homework. The course content is so tough, the project is so heavy, and pen-paper exam for coding?? INCREDIBLE

Only take this course if you want to lose your sanity. Extremely boring and unhelpful lectures with 5% for attendance. Assignment every 2 weeks which are no where related to class slides. A pen and paper based midterm exam where he expects us to pretend to be a compiler. The exam was lengthy and unable to finish within time.

analysis.name: Yeonju Jang
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took her FINA3301 class. It was 3 exams, 2 group projects, and some hw assignments. Practice exams are helpful; the exams aren't too bad (Canvas in-person exams). Attendance is mandatory (3 absences allowed) and lectures are pretty boring (mostly reading off slides) but overall not a bad experience. Group work is very tedious

I loved her class! I am by no means any finance genius but she truly did care about my success and was always available during her office hours. Her tests were tough but she curves grades at the end of the semester! As long as you come to class and put the work in you will do great!

Really great professor! Course content was extremely clear. Slides had all the information you needed to master for exams. Her exams were fair and based off of the many in class practice problems we worked through together. She also provides practice tests before exams that reflect the difficulty of the actual test.

She's a super nice person, but her exams are hard in the way that it's super conceptual and challenging. She's a great person, but I just couldn't find a way to do well in her class despite visiting her in office hours and studying forever.

I took Prof Jang's FINA3303 class and she's very knowledgeable and a caring professor but it's such a difficult class! Be sure to study hard and go to her office hours. She's very generous with grading overall which is appreciated!

analysis.name: John Wegner
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

"Three unexcused absences will

I have never seen a syllabus with such strict policies (specifically for attendance). Also the fact that this intro to fonts course gives more work than any of my 4-credit class... If I had a time machine, I would go back to the add-drop period and remove typographic systems from my schedule.
lectures are boring . thinks too highly of himself
John is nice! He gives back what you put in

analysis.name: Ilter Bakkal
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

review_highlights.comment: He is a terrible teacher, although the subject matter was really interesting to me. He is very unhelpful even when you go to his office hours and ask him directly for clarification. I would recommend taking this course with someone else.

Very old fashioned - uses chalkboard to teach. He clearly cared deeply about environmental economics, so he always had a lot to say. Not a lot of hw assignments, and he's an easy enough grader. Can be hard to follow at times bc of his lecture-heavy style, but if you pay attention you will do just fine. Does often give vague instructions on purpose

Good lord. Where do I begin? I hate this man. He explains things like he doesn't want you to understand them. If you pay attention in class, it is futile. All your attention should be paid to the textbook out of class. He is extremely boring, and by far the worst teacher I have ever met. Be prepared to see points taken off for no reason. Curse you.

Had Bakkal for a Critique of Capitalism class, and most of my concerns came from the way he organized the class.Towards the end of the sem lectures became way more disorganized. Still, he was clear about what terms /questions would be on tests, and as long as you actually listen in lectures and do all readings you will be fine.

As long as you attend his classes you will be fine. He has office hours before classes and his study guides translate very well to the exams. If you can answer all the questions on the study guide you will do well on the test, he is not a harsh grader and the course involves almost no math.

analysis.name: Karl Lieberherr

review_highlights.comment:

- First few weeks are brutal

Probably the worst professor at Northeastern. You cannot understand what he is saying most of the time. The TAs are not helpful and take days to respond to even the most basic questions. Exam averages were around a 50, and weekly assignments take hours to complete.  Avoid this class.

Seriously avoid this class if possible. I took it because I needed a class with a lab for 5 credits and this was offered online. Serious mistake. The assignments are very hard and the professor essentially makes you use AI to learn everything and do the assignments. However, on exams, you cant use AI which makes them very difficult.

By far the worst professor I've had at Northeastern. As someone with ZERO excel experience/knowledge, I took this course thinking it would be an introductory course (1000 course). But, this professor has decided to overcomplicate topics as if we're all experts at CS, designed hellish weekly assignments, and the TAs are unhelpful.

This class is like starving to death. At first, you try and try to make it through the next day, but eventually, your stomach distends, and you hallucinate the laughing specter of Karl, mocking you, as you cannot even muster up the strength to swat the flies off of your face. You, and your GPA die, just as you came into this world, alone.

analysis.name: Shantanu Khanna
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He's one of those professors whose enthusiasm for a subject wears off on you, and you find yourself excited about something as basic as intro stats. His class is lecture-heavy, but so engaging that time flies by. He's available to discuss anything you might be working on outside of class, and he did so happily (most of the time).

Amazing teacher, really wants to help his students. I really enjoyed his class and found him to be one of the best professors I have had at this school. He makes the subject simple and breaks it down so that everyone can understand.

I had him for INSH 6500 which is Statistical Analysis as an in-person class. I did not have a good experience with him, most of the homework took me anywhere from 3 to 6 hours for a maximum of 5 questions. Also, the projects were not good either. It took me and several other people 5-10 hours per project and we'd get different answers to them.

He is one of the best-balanced professors I've taken. Assignment due dates are clearly communicated. The workload is well-structured and manageable. His video lectures are light. The assignments are clear and well-organized, and he gives detailed instructions along with a grading rubric for all writing assignments. I would take his classes again.

Shantanu is a really good prof who cares about you and wants you to do well and will do everything he can to help you get there. His lectures are engaging and is very open to questions. Gives many practice questions for revision and midterms (2) do not contain anything out of practice. HW are usually easy-medium, shout out to TA Dayonara!

analysis.name: Jude Mathews
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 141 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: exam averages were around 65 each time and she never curved. i know maybe 4 people who passed, everyone else i know didn't. avoid at all costs.

One of the good teachers out there. She listens to each student and also goes out of her way to help explain difficult concepts such as NMR. I was expecting an easier class reading reviews from last semester, but definitely do not think so. Prof. Mathews makes Orgo 2 easy to understand and digest! Make sure to attend class and esp. review sessions.

Dr. Mathews is one of the best professors I've ever had. She is extremely clear and tells you what you need to know. Going into Orgo I was definitely worried, but she makes it accessible. In my experience, doing the homework and going to class is essential for doing well on exams, and tutoring is also a great way to reinforce material.

Unprofessional during office hours. I have witnessed her scream at a student for asking a valid question. You should still take the course with her because as awful as her personality is, she makes the material digestible & an A is possible with hard work (you don't need to put in 20 hours a week like she claims, she needs to chill & just retire)

Would not recommend. The teaching style made the material hard to understand, and explanations were unclear. Concepts weren't broken down well. Also, several overly positive reviews appeared before the semester ended—LIKE TWO ON MARCH 19 AND 21, 2025—which seems very suspicious and raises doubts about the class's true quality.

analysis.name: Sagar Kamarthi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Prof Kamarthi was a really nice guy. But the student (IE's) treated him like crap, they complained about everthing. The Tests were straight out of the problems sets he would go over in class and post solutions to on blackboard. What more could you ask for. Course was not what i expected from description but i did Enjoy the lab. Really nice guy!

Prof Kamarthi genuinely wants you to succeed. He opens day one with that and means it. Logical concept order, great TAs, fun free-form final project. Midterms pull directly from practice problems he flags explicitly, plus grade recovery opportunities. Harder to fail than get an A if you show up, pay attention, and give some genuine effort.

Moody and unorganized. Grading has no consistency. If he likes you it will help. Doesn't cover material well. Dives into detail on stuff he knows well but barely skims over stuff he hasn't spent time to learn. Very little passion for teaching.

Horrible. I worked in manuf. on co-op before this class, and i was excited to get into some more details. But his lack of communication and poor teaching left me stunned. Stay away from this class if you can. Who gives students a packet of computer code 20 minutes before class is over and says "learn this for tomorrow's midterm"? Way to 'teach' us.

Very systematic course and Kamarthi teaches it that way. Goes through a cycle of concepts, introduction of equations, practice problems, homework assignments based on concepts learned in class. Kamarthi is a very good professor. A bit dry at times but that could be because material is also dry. Would recommend.

analysis.name: Lynn Li
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

Tests are easy and the class is chill.

You can tell by her lectures that she took time and effort in preparing, in hopes of making the material easy to understand. Though attendance is not mandatory, going to class, paying attention, completing the required homework, and putting in time to understand the material will help you succeed in the course.

I think she's a good professor, but she teaches like we are in middle school and it gets very frustrating. It is hard to focus in her class because she tends to describe things in a way that is way more complex than needed. She is really nice and caring outside of class and answers emails fast.

Good overall, but the lectures can be kind of confusing. Shes caring and understanding, easy to reach. Although attendance is not mandatory, if you don't go to class youll get pretty lost. Organized and clear instructions/grading.
It was the best class at northeastern that I have ever taken. Exams are very easy if you study well. Gives good feedback, replies to email in seconds. Perfect professor at NEU.

analysis.name: Steven Lopez

i dropped this class and am retaking it with jude matthews, best decision ever. it seems like professor lopez has gotten worse since i last had him, which was already quite bad. i can't wait to take my orgo final where i now have the confidence + knowledge to ace it. i highly recommend you all to get a different professor, do not rely on the curve!

Really nice but hard to learn in his class since he seems confused about what he's teaching sometimes, better off self-studying.

Way too opinionated grading. Dont take puts off for not explaining the answer when the question doesn't say explain(Especially when you dont for other questions!). Way too harsh a grader for no reason. The content is almost middle school level, and she grades way too harshly for what it is.

Very difficult class because of the way she chooses to grade, we clearly understand concepts, but so that everyone doesn't get A she grades very tough, which is also heavily specific/even at times opinionated.

analysis.name: Lee Moreau
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: he is the best of all the design lecturers. okay the lectures are long, and he does give lots of reading, but for the most part it is all fairly interesting, and you can def grasp the points by skimming through/showing up to class most of the time. overall he is very accomplished in the design world but still lighthearted and approachable. easy A.

lee is great, and you can tell he is knowledgeable when it comes to design perspectives. attendence every class gets old after the first week, especially since the guest speakers werent always the most interesting/relevant. it is also just a very long block of time to sit in a lecture hall. a little too serious for a 2credit course, but not awful.

Another foundational design course similar to most of the foundation courses. The material feels redundant, especially the hw. The discussions are easy to write, but the seminar for this class is pretty boring and overwhelming with busy work. Another example of how CAMD needs major curriculum reformation. Would never take this class willingly.

guest speakers are irrelevant sometimes, but attendance is mandatory regardless of major and interest, which is fine but a bit annoying. Very repetitive assignments, gets tiring, lecture hall is the worst room in the building, such cramped inconvenient seating, and he keeps making people get up and move around and its really such a hassle

One of my favorite professors so far. Lectures were engaging and featured guest speakers with fresh povs. Studio felt like an open, collaborative space that made it easy to stay involved. Projects were flexible and allowed us to explore our interests, which made the work genuinely enjoyable.

analysis.name: Getty Lustila

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Lustilla is the best professor I've ever had. Both discussions and coursework are extremely thought-provoking and interesting! Discussions are very open and unbiased, and he takes the time to thoughtfully work through everyone's considerations. He honestly just cares about his students and wants them to learn and succeed. Take this class!

He's genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had-- super laid-back, his priority is having students actually engage with the material. He also very clearly cares and wants to get to know his class. If you haven't had a chance, definitely take a class with prof Lustila!

Professor Lustila is super kind, caring, chill, and funny. He's very passionate about philosophy and extremely knowledgable in regards to the material being taught. Class time is just a discussion based off of the readings that are really interesting and genuinely get you thinking.

My favorite human and my favorite professor at Northeastern. Every time I went to class I learned something new about life and about myself. He is brilliant and kind and everything desirable in a philosophy professor. I am so thankful I was able to learn from him.

If you want a class where the prof is extremely passionate and knowledgable about the material, this is the one for you. I took Indigenous Philosophy during the first semester it was offered, and it was my favorite class by far. Getty is hilarious, his readings are very accessible, and he totally opened my mind to all sorts of new ways of thinking.

Great person who truly cares about his student's succeeding. He is always more than happy to answer any questions students may have, and thoroughly goes through problems in class. analysis.name: Michael Ruff

He gives projects and hw (unlimited tries) to balance grades. The final exam is extremely hard, be prepared to study a lot. You can survive the class, wont be easy.

Professor ruff, is overall a great guy. However, he is a really tuff grader. His exams, while mainly multiple choice are extremely hard. I attended every class, went to office hours and saw the TA and still struggled.  He over complicates the subjects and is heavily power point based.

Prof Ruff is a great dude, not the best teacher by any means, but a great guy. analysis.name: William Mayer

review_highlights.comment: The class was graded on two quizzes and a midterm, but as long as you take notes during class you'll be totally fine. If you miss a day get notes from a friend. Very very nice professor who tried to connect with all students in the class. Lectures made up the entire class and was him talking the whole time. Literally the funniest man ever. Loved his dry humor, but also he would drone on in lectures. Very hard to pay attention to. He speaks with a lot of long pauses in btwn sentences and is not super clear when doing practice problems. Hard to follow, accent made it a little bit harder as well. But he cares how students do and wants them to succeed.

analysis.name: Zachary Agatstein
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Agatstein cares so much about his students, explains things clearly, gives relevant examples, is very understanding about giving extensions + grades kindly. He would have a class every couple of weeks dedicated to letting us access his knowledge + ask him about things going on in the world from an IR perspective. Best professor I've had.

He's super chill. The class was weekly essays, and the same went for the final project. He's a really fair grader and was super understanding. Definitely a great online course, and managed everything well.
He was a super understanding and fair professor. If you are to take an online course for political science take his. I've never had such an organized professor, nevermind being online. Great guy.

Professor Agatstein is an intelligent, organized, and kind professor. Overall, if you are looking for a good, chill class with a Professor who knows his stuff, take his class!! He is excellent at considering each student's needs while being fair to the entire class. His specialty in humanitarian crises is fascinating.

I have never rated a professor before, but I have to, for Dr. Agatstein was amazing. I loved his discussions, as they were always interesting and relevant. He doesn't force you to reply. All assignments are argumentative essays, which I love. He responds quickly and gives great constructive feedback. Great class to take for NU Path or for credit.

analysis.name: Christina Agostinelli-Fucile
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Do not take this class with her if you are a STEM major or have ANY other demanding classes! I was taking Orgo at the same time and I genuinely feel like she lowered me a letter grade by requiring 2+ hours of my time every night doing homework, projects, or essays. However, the class will definitely improve your Spanish speaking and writing!

Professor Agostinelli-Fucile is a good professor. The class (advanced Spanish II) is pretty much all in Spanish. There is a good amount of writing for homework but as long as you do it, you get full credit for it. There is a lot of conversation and she calls on you if you don't talk much. Make sure you come to class prepared.

She is nice, accessible outside of class, & willing to reexplain concepts during office hours. Authentic Spanish Grammar was a difficult class b/c the material was high-level & could be complicated, plus there were a lot of assignments, essay, videos, & readings, but tbh I didn't read everything & still did fine. It's a summer course so fastpaced.

Her special topics spanish classes are hybrid classes, so half online half in person. Her RISE lectures are super detailed & contain a lot of links & videos. You definitely learn a lot of material but it's a project-based class so no tests or memorization. She can be a picky grader but if u go to her office hours & do what she says you'll get an A.

Do not listen to comments that say that she gives too much homework!! This was the BEST SPANISH CLASS AT NORTHEASTERN. I cant even tell you how much I learned, the flip classroom is great and there are so many assignments that nothing will kill your grade. This is not an easy A,(but not hard!) it's a class if you truly want to improve your Spanish.

analysis.name: Rajesh Aggarwal
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Excellent professor. One of the most engaging classes I have taken at Northeastern. It was helpful that the students in my class were also excellent and asked questions frequently. Class material is straightforward and requires critical thinking. Teaches you more than just the fundamentals of finance. Would take any class he teaches in the future

Aggarwal made me want to go to an 8am class. His lecture style is engaging and he is clearly a master at what he teaches. His class is not easy but if you attend his lectures (which are not mandatory) you will be fine. His exams are difficult but they are open note, you can use excel (which is extremely helpful), and there is a heavy curve.

He is so passionate about the subject and I learned a lot about finance from this course. You won't know your final grade in the course until the end, the curves are approximated so you may have a rough idea but will not have a true estimate until the end. Takes the time to genuinely answer any and all student questions, this was my favorite class!

A+ professor! I have never found a professor who cares as much about the subject as he does and is as passionate as he is. wifi issues during the final which many people will rate him poorly for, but it was not his fault, and these people are just upset they did poorly on the final and trying to find an excuse. Take him if you want to learn!

SO SO passionate about finance and really knows his shit. Exams are hard though they've got a sweet curve. Probably the only 8am I consistently attended. Take him if you actually want to learn. What an incredible guy.

analysis.name: Adeel  Bhutta
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class itself is very heavily project based, and one midterm. Bhutta is a good prof, but his lectures are a bit monotonous at times. A lot of things in the class require more practice on your own time, and the projects do take a while, so don't make the same mistake I did about procrastination. Overall, good prof but the course itself is hard.

There is a ton of work and not a lot of leniency. I understand that the Professor expects 20+ hours of time commitment per week for quality learning, but the EXTREMELY harsh grading criteria and little to no exceptions given make it very difficult for students with obligations outside of the class. If you have another class or worse, a job, then GL

I had the pleasure of taking your CS3520 during Summer 2024. Throughout the course, I consistently attended TA office hours to deepen my understanding and improve my programming skills, and I greatly appreciated the support and guidance from the course staff. Course was both challenging and rewarding, significantly enhancing my proficiency in C++.

It's an insane amount of work if you have responsibilities outside of this class. It's nonsensical as to why so much work is assigned each week. I find myself constantly trying to finish the assignments rather than learning and absorbing the material. I'd try to avoid this class if you aren't good at time management.

It was a great semester. I genuinely learnt so much from this class, and it was one of my favorite CS classes. I have grown so much as a person having learnt the skills that I did in this class. I appreciated all of the lectures very much, so thank you Professor Bhutta for giving us such a wholistic view of software engineering.

analysis.name: John Adams
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr Adams is pretty mean. Whenever his students are having difficulties due to his sloppy teaching style, he'll outwardly call them out and moan his frustrations when he's the one who can't teach effectively. His lectures are awfuland all over the place usually not including things that are on the hw. Dont listen to the other reviews. Dont take him.

Dr. Adams is amazing. Great teacher and a great person. He is the best professor I've had at Northeastern so far. The lectures are engaging even when there is a lot of information to cover. He is always happy to answer questions. His tests are fair and based on the slides and the quizzes. There are no surprises.

If you can't handle his mildly inappropriate jokes that he makes because we are all ADULTS... go back to middle school. His sense of humour and ability to connect to us makes this class so much easier to understand and way more bearable. Attendance is HUGE, and so is something called SPSS.

If you're taking considering taking Dr. Adams, you totally should! Although attendance is mandatory, it is literally impossible not to get an A in this class since it is worth 30% of your grade. I enjoyed going to his class at 8am since he is very engaging and knows the subject well. I promise, he is super approachable and an overall great prof!

He can't clearly communicate to students and lecture slides are confusing. Homework's helpful, but you kinda have to reteach yourself everything since he speeds through lectures and doesn't emphasize important info. Also dropped a huge exam on us after realizing he forgot to test us basically the whole semester and just overcomplicated the course.

analysis.name: Adam Marks
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Adam was great. He kept class as entertaining as he could and would let us out early. All the quizzes were at home online and there was no final exam. Workload was light. He does take attendance but very understanding.
Best professor i've had at Northeastern for SURE. A must take. He cares and you learn things that you actually will use.
Good guy. He's super understanding. Class isn't super hard. A 2.0 in difficulty sounds about right.

analysis.name: Adam Cooper
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: ling2350 was the hardest class i took last year. very tedious work which was cool in the end, but so time consuming. very niche in depth papers ~biweekly but u get very detailed feedback and peer editing time etc. hes very nice but so so boring i fell asleep. so knowledgable id recommend taking one of his classes at least onc

Intro to Ling can be tedious--it is a hard subject to teach and a lot of other people are taking the class for credit and aren't very interested. For all other Ling classes, I have only good things to say about the course content and Dr. Cooper--caring, well-respected, accessible, provides thoughtful answers to questions, opportunity for extra cred

Prof. Cooper was great! He's very knowledgeable in linguistics and wants to share his love for the subject with his students. Our class (through the Explore Program) covered intro topics not in much detail but it was still interesting to learn about and I looked forward to our classes. Assignments are reasonable and fun to complete - I recommend!

It's been a while since I took a class with him, but I needed to leave a review because Cooper is the GOAT. He is super knowledgeable, his lectures are always well thought-out and run smoothly, he's a really fair grader, accessible outside of class, and he's funny. People need to appreciate this prof more because he's the best in the department.

Dr. Cooper is a wonderful professor! He makes his material accessible and interesting, I always looked forward to class with him. He will pay attention to student feedback; helped make the class environment feel unified and provided a platform for everyone to participate.  Class with him was fun, insightful, and productive.

analysis.name: Adonis Antoniades
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Adonis is an amazing professor. He cares about his students and genuinely wants them to do well. He can be strict sometimes, but it's because he cares. There were 2 20 question midterms and a 10 question final, non cumulative. Very interesting content and he definitely has been one of my favorite professors. Take this class if you can get a seat.

good professor. really cares about what he's teaching, and wants his students to learn and understand. strict in class, makes up for it with bad dad jokes. class is mostly determined by midterms and final. covers a lot of content, from residential to commercial while including legal. test questions are also incredibly specific. review all slides

A great professor!! Super passionate about the class & really wants you to learn. The class is difficult, but if you put in the work it will be rewarding. Homework, case deliverables, & finance in practices are all groups assignments so make sure to get a good group at the beginning. There is midterm & final of 20 mc question & get a ref sheet.

Prof. Antoniades is a bit of a hardo in that he expects a lot out of his students, but if you put in the work you will be well rewarded. He's a great teacher and a super nice guy. All work is group work so make sure you know someone in your class/meet people early. Once you get used to his style this course is not too difficult and youll learn lots

One of the best profs at Northeastern. Cares about his students and subject matter a lot. Class isn't easy but nothing too bad and he makes expectations clear plus is very willing to help. He is also a very clear lecturer and goes to great lengths to make sure that everyone is on the same page.

analysis.name: Adebukola Ajao
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Pretty disorganized prof. Rarely gives feedback for work which makes it difficult to understand how to do better. Not really helpful in communication. Waits until the last moment to post important info about projects. When she does post, its very short and lacks detail, unlike other profs. Doesn't seem like she really knows how to be a prof.

horrible professor. not only does she not actually teach anything (no lectures/ppts/videos/etc.), she is rude and dismissive over email. not once have i gotten a real and useful email response from her. i have never had a professor this bad at neu. if there's another prof available for digital marketing, take the other professor

analysis.name: Karen Aerni
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very helpful in class and led very interesting lectures which helped make the curriculum feel accessible. Grades pretty easy and makes her rubrics for projects very understandable. Participation is very important in her classes, but you can choose to attend through Zoom instead of in person. Hard to reach outside of class except in office hours.

The class was great, you got out of it what you put into it. Lecture-heavy, easy homework, professor very understanding, personable and smart. Participation graded but you were able to attend class virtually. Only problem would be that she is a little hard to reach outside of class/by email. overall would recommend and I want to be her friend

Loved her class, can be attended online or in person. Lectures are engaging and educational, and in class she is very helpful with questions/concerns. Only issue is she is very difficult to reach outside of class, never got an email back. Many opportunities for your grade, optional extra credit final and projects have super clear rubrics.

ENVR1400- Goes pretty fast through the slides but if you pay attention you will be fine, and lab is important for this course. She's really nice and personable but takes a while to grade sometimes. Canvas can be unorganized but she will always move due dates back if you express you had online issues. Participation required but you can join on zoom.

Held lectures on zoom and in person at the same time(you can still attend classes while sick in bed), great lecturer and easy to take notes for. Class content was easy. Dr. Aerni was very friendly and helpful in one-on-one interactions, came across as someone who genuinely wants students to learn and enjoy classes.

analysis.name: Aeshna Badruzzaman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Badruzzaman's lectures might seem a bit rushed, but she is very sweet and genuinely cares about all of her students. She's not the easiest grader in the world but she is fair, and she gives plenty of notice for deadlines and things of that sort. International Relations with her was term-heavy, but she's more than willing to help if you asked.

Probably the best professor I have had at Northeastern so far. She is kind, a great lecturer and a very fair grader. She takes attendance and keeps track of participation, but you can get credit for this from in-class writings every class. I got credit for every in-class writing without even reading the material. DON'T BUY THE TEXTBOOKS

Dr. B is one of the best professors I have ever had. I originally took her international relations class as a poli sci major and loved it so much I switched to IA. She is a gem! Has so many office hours, very passionate, always makes class engaging, and does an amazing job explaining IR theories. If you get the chance to take IR with her, do it.

Dr. B is a great lecturer though you have to make sure to keep up with her pace. The course is graded from two non-cumulative exams, a paper, and a group presentation. She's super accessible and understanding with students though you need to make sure to keep up with attendance or it will affect your grade.

analysis.name: Laurel Ahnert
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: as someone taking this as an elective, it was great there wasn't much work. you only need to do 5/10 discussion posts and 3 exams. however, this course is 100% memorization, which is time consuming to study for the exams. overall, she made the lectures interesting, even at times when the content wasn't.

lectures are well paced and thought out, wish we got to engage more since its such a large lecture. i have a brain that prefers smaller classes, but i am (for the most part) easily focused in her lectures even tho they are huge. chill class though not too much work. go to the lectures though, your attendance is graded

Media Culture and Society was a very interesting class. It was a large lecture so I wasn't expecting it to be the most engaging, but Prof Ahnert was a great speaker and listening was never monotonous. She provided a clear study guide before the 2 multiple-choice exams.

Professor Ahnert wasn't very good at giving clear instructions with projects and essays, and would just take off a bunch of points after during grading. Her classes were very boring, but attendance was mandatory. She never gave feedback also after taking points off, like she took 8 points off and wrote "good work" and didn't give feedback.

Prof Ahnert is a really respectable person. The course was pretty straight forward, but 75% of the course was based on 3 exams, so that isn't great when the exams are 25 questions each. Overall a great prof who gives detailed info about the courses she teaches.

analysis.name: Adenekan Dedeke
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 86 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's not horrible but proceed with caution. He's very knowledgable and passionate about MIS. It's also clear he cares about his students. However, his canvas page is a mess, he makes diagnostic quizzes due at 7am, and his exams are brutal (gives a curve). If you take him, go in with your guns blazing, and he will respect the effort.

Honestly I don't get the hate? Some people say he's hard to understand-- I didn't encounter this problem. DQs due by 7am for most classes (like 5 question quiz based on reading, not hard). Random groups given in beginning of semester you have to complete occasional HWs with. Tests are hard because its content heavy MCQ + boring lectures & subject

Here's how you do well in this class: Sit in the front and participate. You will hear Dr. Nick clearly, he will learn your name, and he will give you opportunities to answer questions. You MUST pay attention. If you want to sit in the back and half-listen, don't expect to do well. Lectures are boring but it's up to you to make something of it.

Honestly, I think Dedeke is over-hated. He puts in effort to make lectures less boring, even though the content itself is pretty dry. I didn't do great on the exams, but I still got an A thanks to the curve and tons of extra credit. Overall, if you have a group with at least 3 responsible guy and do the practice exams, dw you'll be fine.

Despite it being an online class, deliverables are due every Wednesday and Saturday night, and assignments are locked to the Monday or Thursday before, respectively, only giving 3 days for every assignment, no matter the length. This becomes a huge issue in group projects in an asynchronous setting where your groupmates are unresponsive. Beware.

analysis.name: Ahmet Coskun
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is an amazing professor. Despite somewhat heavy lectures overall, you can do it very well with his lecture notes and his discussion. His subjects are also worthwhile to take. He is also willing to discuss during office hours. I can say he is an incredible professor who is good to students and good at teaching.

Coskun is a solid choice. There isn't a better option than him so might as well take him. I never attended the lectures and still got a good grade because of the textbook. He prerecords all his lectures so you can take it fully asynchronously if you want. His lectures are very detailed PowerPoints so they are a good reference. Class concepts hard.

awesome class, of course, for engineering majors. i enjoyed it, he was very clear on what he wanted and laid everything out for us so material was relatively easy to learn as long as you just paid attention and showed up. always in a good mood. didnt mind if i played computer games on my downtime. looked forward to class.

Coskun is an amazing professor. Thermo is an extremely hard course with difficult concepts and his lectures do a great job of making it understandable. He is super nice and easy to find after class and is very good about answering question. Also hes just an absolute savage so gotta love coskun.

He uses Power Point heavily in lectures, but that is actually very helpful because you can easily see the correct equations without trying to understand handwriting. I went to his office hours several times and he was very helpful and also gave good feedback on the Midterms.

analysis.name: Amal Ahmed
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: only lectures worth coming are new topics. homework is 10 times harder than the lectures. please get lucky with your partner or be ready to do all your work by yourself. come to office hours a lot. final project (similar topic with her research i assume) was useless - try to do good on your homeworks so that you can skip one at the end.

As mentioned by the other reviewers, it's not required to go to lectures, but if you choose to skip on lectures, you'll need to read the textbook. I never touched the textbook and entirely went to lectures. The homework is tough but doable and very rewarding. Overall, she's an engaging lecturer so pay attention and you'll be fine.

I loved Amal! She was super passionate about the material. Her lectures did get a little boring near the end of the semester, but that was more of me being burnt out. If you want a good grade, make sure you show up to lectures. The homework got REALLY tough near the end of the year, but if you stick with it you'll do fine.

Really animated teacher. Keeps the lectures interesting and explains everything well. The problem setsexams are tough for some but the TAs are always there to help.  Textbook reading is unnecessary, lectures and problem sets cover all you'll need to know.
I really enjoyed Amal's class. She was chill and very patient. Her class was very interesting. You have to pay attention to lectures and work hard on homework to receive good grades.

analysis.name: Jaehan Ahn
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Ahn is an amazing, respectful teacher. His lectures are clear, the course Canvas page is organized, he gives review materials for each chapter, and he offers consistent office hours. The course has two midterms, each worth 15%, a final worth 30%, four quizzes worth 10%, connect homework assignments, participation, and a project.

Professor Ahn is the best professor that I have had at Northeastern so far. He is clearly very knowledgable about the material, passionate for teaching, and super kind. He grades generously and fairly. The class itself is pretty difficult but Professor Ahn gives you all the tools needed to succeed and all tests/quizzes are curved.

A great professor for grading—quizzes get a nice curve, but exams don't. Lectures can be dull, but that's just the class. He's kind with selective office hours. Given accounting's difficulty, he grades generously. Multiple choice is key on exams, making up half the quiz points. Struggling? Watch Tony Bell's FA videos—they match the class perfectly.

Accounting in general is a hard course so I can't hate too much. Professor Ahn was great at first. His quizzes were okay and he went through content slowly. When we got to the more difficult chapters, he went too fast for my liking. Very exam heavy! However, he is kind and welcoming and made an effort to get to known everyone's names.

Professor Ahn is a wonderful professor to take. He made Accounting clear and understandable whilst also providing useful background experience. Grading is generous and you will do fine provided you understand the assigned homework. I wish he could teach my second accounting course here.

analysis.name: Aaron Daniels
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Daniels is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is incredibly knowledgeable and uses his experience in the field to great effect in lectures. Bi-weekly essays are intimidating, but he has a specific formula that you can follow to easily get a good grade. If you ever have the chance, PLEASE take a class with him. you won't regret it.

Such a kind, engaging professor who truly cares about helping students connect with the material. Lectures can be long, but discussions are fascinating. He offers plenty of extra credit, gives great feedback, and his office hours are super helpful (but fill up fast!). My favorite professor—also take his Clinical Psych class if you can.

Professor Daniels is easily my favorite professor at Northeastern. I've had many great profs, but I have learned the most from his classes. Don't be scared by the writing assignments and lectures; he is extremely fair. Lectures are hilarious and engaging; he is exceedingly passionate and knowledgeable, just a wonderful and compassionate person.

Be careful, this might be the best professor you'll ever have. Whatever you do, don't be intimated by the 30 page syllabus this class is a blast and made me excited to wake up in the mornings. He also lets you attend his meditations for extra credit which was really cool. Enjoy!

Yes, 8am for this course is WORTH IT! I've learned so much. Grading: 50% papers, 25% participation, 25% attendance. Syllabus: is literal art(it's thorough). Email for Office hours appointment EARLY ON to get feedback on paper before the deadline(fills up fast). Lots of extra credit opportunities! No final, just a presentation.

analysis.name: Aatmesh Shrivastava
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Explained concepts poorly, poor presentations, was not approachable.
Genuine goat. He has so much to teach you, if you actually engage the class, and he genuinely wants you to succeed. Best prof ive had so far.
Often provides interesting insights about circuits and their in real world.

Challenging but covers a niche subject rarely offered at colleges. Half the course focused on linear regulators, then jumped to various topics in the last month; combined with the project made things hard to follow, but talking with the prof helped clarify topics and HWs. Very lecture heavy too. Critique: late to post grades/solutions

analysis.name: Ahmad Saranjam
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: saranjam on toast is HILARIOUS. he says funny things like that the shoes he bought were "twice money" and "bagels the size of pizza." so classic. i spent most of class drawing and writing down his quotes and still got a good grade. ahmad is really straight forward and loves to ask rhetorical questions that nobody answers-but it's ok, he's adorable.

I took him last semster and he stopped giving the answers to the midterm and final ahead of time ... but there are online quizzes and the midterm was really easy (only 7 q's) but the final was really hard but much harder than midterm) however class is easy and he gives you an extra credit option im a poli sci major and this was an easy econ class

This man is my life. He's hot, he's hilarious, and he knows it secretly. Sexy accent; it's like having Santa Claus teach me (plus some Owl and Cat like features). His class is fun and straightforward and he makes jokes that he giggles at (because they're hilarious). He uses GM in all of his "Exam-Pail"s. Love. him. Hope he's single <333333333

This guy knows his stuff and makes the class pretty easy by only teaching basics. His teaching style is very clear and the classes are all notes on the board except when he asks questions and no one answers; then he answers himself. The tests are all based on the notes and for midterm and final he gives you the questions to do before the test.

All he does is lecture. What he teaches is identical to what's in the book, so a lot of people don't go to class, and just study from the book and do fine on the quizzes. Extra credit essays add ten points to each quiz grade if you have the time to do them. Midterm & Final were easy essay questions taken straight from the chapter reviews.

analysis.name: Aarti Sathyanarayana
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She was the second professor in this class, which should have just been one professor. She would rush through slide shows and often talk herself into circles when trying to explain a concept. Attendance does count as extra credit but the lectures are not worth it.

She was our joint professor for PHTH 2210. She was unable to answer questions and  often speed through an entire lesson in 45 minutes when class is double that. She is also hard to reach outside of class.

By far the best class I have taken! Professor Aarti shows so much care for her students. Her grading is very fair and the projects are incredibly useful for both resume and learning through supplemental resources. She is open to new ideas and has helped me get to a level of programming in the data science realm that I never knew I would achieve!

Professor Sathyanarayana understood the challenges of being a beginner in coding and brought lots of practical applications to the teachings in DS 2000. I often found that our assignments had more than enough time, and class periods were used to meet with TAs or ask her any questions. So knowledgeable and positive, truly wants her students to learn

Assignments given in class didn't align with the corequisite course (DS2000); I had to seek help from TAs for almost every hw. Final project was very tedious, but she gave good feedback during early stages and was a relatively fair grader. She's willing to assist students outside of class, but overall it was too difficult for an entry level course.

analysis.name: Aaron  Daniels
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Daniels is an amazing professor. I have taken two classes with him and love his lecturing style. His course is all paper-based (no tests), so if that works better for you, I 100% recommend him. The papers are challenging, but he gives thoughtful feedback for each one. His assignments are very thought-provoking, which I enjoyed.

I absolutely loved this class. He is such an intelligent professor and makes the content so interesting. I am willing taking another class at 8:00 am because he is the professor. He's that good. If you don't like to write, this class might not be for you: your grade is based off of 5 or 6 papers you work on throughout the semester.

This is the second class I took with Professor Daniels, and I enjoyed it just as much as I did the first one. He is very well-educated in his field and a great professor. His class is paper-based (6 throughout the semester), so if you enjoy writing, take him! The topics covered are interesting, and he is a great lecturer.

analysis.name: Aaron Roth
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

analysis.name: Doug Bielmeier
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Doug is an incredible professor on music. It's a lot of labs, group project work, and quizzes, but he is lenient on grading and he caters to those who may not be music majors or have background knowledge in ProTools. Loved his class for Recording 1 and 2!

Dr. Doug is great. One goal I had for this course was to learn more about music recording so I could apply it to my own personal, musical endeavors and continue to improve my skills. I achieved my goal over the course of the semester because I was able to take everything I learned and apply to one of my own songs for our final project.

Seeing as the course is over, a goal that I had for the course was to get better at making sure everything feels like it's sitting in the mix rather than on top of it. I think that I have gotten significantly better at this by changing the way I EQ each track. Dr. Doug sets up the class for future producers to be successful.

Doug Bielmeier really brought his job as a mix engineer to fruition in my mind. He's very understanding of his students when they have "off-day" and doesn't hesitate to accommodate our needs to the best of his ability. He's great at answering questions in a well communicated manner and he's quite charismatic as well.

I really enjoyed having Dr. Doug as a professor. He was incredibly knowledgable and passionate about various aspects of Music Recording. He personalized each lecture in order to make an easygoing and enjoyable atmosphere. I felt comfortable reaching out if I had questions because of his down-to-earth teaching approach

analysis.name: Bilge Erten
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

Easy HWs & EASY MIDTERM and a final.

Prof Erten Is nice and knowledgable, but as someone who has never taken an econ class before, this class was difficult and challenging, and at times the class moved too quickly to follow. Many other students in this class already have quite a bit of knowledge in Econ. The midterm was good, but final was hard.

Interesting class. Grad professor teaching an intro Macro course was really cool and I learned a lot. She's a great teacher and obviously knows what she's talking about. A lot nicer to have her in a 49 person class rather than Simon in a 200 person lecture hall.

analysis.name: Gwen Bindas

She's not clear at all and even one on one help is completely useless. She does not make helpful revisions. I have legitimately not learned a single thing in this class. Class is completely unrelated to the assignments. If she likes you, you'll get an A. If she doesn't want to give you an A, forget about it.

An Amazing professor. Very calm and extremely lenient with assignments and quiz. Always there to help during the project work. Extremely approachable and it was fun to attend his class. Very knowledgeable and highly talented in his field. If you get ERM just take it and enjoy :)
Most boring lectures I have ever been in. Outdated lectures and disorganized. Assignments are vague and busy work.

Very good professor, kind and fair

Amazing time in Calc 2. Came in super rusty on all fronts, but really enjoyed the class and felt like I learned quite a bit. analysis.name: Bill Lancaster

Extremely considerate of your circumstances. His grading is clear and manageable. Just get your projects/papers done and you'll receive the maximum grade. He often compliments students work and uses student examples which makes writing enjoyable.

Professor Huggins is a super nice guy who really helped me learn more about English without additional stress as an Engineering major. His class was pretty easy as long as you tried. I'd 100% recommend taking him!
This is the writing class you want to take. Not too taxing but you still feel like you learned something.

Best professor ive had yet . Very chill guy and gives really good feedback . Went into the class not expecting much but left with so much more . analysis.name: Nathan Blake

Prof Blazek is really nice and cares about his students! I learned a lot in this course and would take him again. Homework, practice exams, and group office hours were really helpful! He's the best professor I had at northeastern. Clearly knowledgable and cares about his students. Super friendly and is always willing to help with homework. Lectures are easy to follow and always posted on canvas. Gives lots of practice material. Likes to do demonstrations.

The prof is awful, I was at a high A and but my final grade was something else. He did not disclose as to what my grades are for participation and negotiation. All my efforts went to waste.

this class made me not like drawing anymore. assignments are repetitive & the sketchbook homework was time-consuming & did not teach me much. she prides herself on giving feedback, but most of the time her suggestions are so vague and not helpful, and when grading homework she will often give a low grade with few words instructing on how to improve

I am a professional baseball player. It was  great class given the hectic traveling and schedule with games.
Professor was always available and I Ieaened a lot, got an A..

Professor Bordbar is a rare find who wants the best for us, makes himself available even after the course closes.
