This class does need good study habits for the final/midterm, but it is manageable because, across the board, she sets very clear expectations for tests/projects. I loved this class!

There was technically a lot to read for this class, however I did not find them all necessary. The class is lecture heavy, but I found them engaging and she gave us a break in the middle of class. She is not always the most clear with what she wants but she is very flexible and understanding. I loved this class and would take it again!

The class is lecture-heavy, but as long as you show up and pay attention, the midterms and finals are easy. She is very understanding about extensions. The rubric for the final project is not very clear, but she is a lenient grader. I really liked her as a professor, and her lectures were interesting.

Professors Brothers is an amazing professor that has a deep passion for architecture and that was evident in her course. While her Canvas page is not the greatest and her organization could be better, she compensates her digital ability with her information packed lecture slides. I would recommend this class to anyone!

Professor Brothers seems passionate about her work and the history but she also doesn't seem to do much work as she has 3 TA's for her class and I notice they do most of the work such as the grading and etc... besides the lecturing. 3 different TAs had separate grading styles and who knows what you'll get for your grades back.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Britt
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She does not use a normal grading system. Professor Britt grades only earned based on quality, and students have to meet every single requirement in her criteria in order to get an A or B. There is also a ton of homework and a huge chunk of time this class takes outside of class. Pick a god and start praying if this is a required class.

Professor Britt really makes you work for a good grade in this class, but she makes it clear what she wants and gives great feedback.  If you pay attention in class + participate and go to her office hours to discuss her comments on your work, you'll do fine.  Building in time to go to office hours is a necessity for this class.
LOOOOOOVE professor britt!! this was the second class i had w her and could not recommend her enough. she is so smart, gives you so many opportunities to improve your work, and you learn a lot.

Professor Britt gives great feedback and is clear about each assignment. Attendance and completing the readings is mandatory since she cold calls to ask about the reading at the beginning of each class. Although your grade relies heavily on the one semester paper, she makes sure you are prepared and have been working on it throughout so it isnt bad

Britt is an excellent professor. She's intelligent, knowledgable, approachable, and on top of her game. She's a tough grader, but she will help you get the A. Listen to all of her suggestions, and your writing will improve 10 fold. She's not a lawyer, but she does have her Ph.D. Anything she doesn't know, she will look up and have the next day. A+

analysis.name: Brianne Olivieri-Mui
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: professor mui is a solid professor. i am historically terrible at epidemiology/statistics but she explained things in a way i understood. she is really nice and she even brought her dog to class once. if you slack off, your grade will suffer, but she does want people to do well and is available for office hours and gives a lot of graded assignments

She is a great professor, and I think everyone is too sensitive. Yes, her class is difficult, but it's meant to be, and it's not her fault. Any comments on her being passive-aggressive are wrong in my opinion. She is honest, and maybe a little awkward sometimes, but I don't think that means she's mean. I loved her and thought she was a total badass
Super funny and awesome sauce.
Not a warm or friendly personality
Very harsh grader, lots of expectations, not very understanding

analysis.name: Chris Bruell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Bruell is a really good teacher and lecturer. His class can be a bit boring and feel repetitive (especially if you've already done criminology in the past), but he has a talent for sparkling debates in class about various subjects. Even though participation is not graded (but attendance is, be careful), he still manages to get people engaged.

Provides all the materials you need to thoroughly understand the material. Homework is weekly and takes some time, but not unmanageable. Midterm and final are open-book, open-note with 4.5 hours to finish (more than enough time). Be careful of the methods you use, he WILL accuse you of cheating if they aren't what you were taught in class.

Professor Bruell is a gem—engaging, organized, and deeply knowledgeable. He blends humor with sensitivity, especially on tough topics. Once, during a domestic violence unit, he bought out a student's donut fundraiser supporting survivors and shared them with the class, saying, “Actions speak louder than words."

He is such a great professor. I had him for CRIM 5900 online over the summer and I learned so much. The class was a lot of reading and work, but it was worth it! He is very approachable and knowledgeable. Take a class with him if you can!
Would do an in class assignment and day “it wasn't in depth enough” but then when more information was added, still said it wasn't enough. The length of the final was not that clear either.

analysis.name: Jeremy Bushnell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely one of the best professors Ive had, I really hope I get him again for more advanced courses. Sometimes Id head to the classroom early to use the empty space to study, and on days when he'd arrive early as well we would talk about all sorts of funny and interesting stuff. He's awesome, please take him, pay attention and you'll learn tons.

He was super caring and really easy to talk to. If you ever have any concerns, you can talk to him right after class or send him an email and he'll respond quickly (within a day). His grading is different from high school English, but he outlines his grading system within the first week and I honestly preferred it over traditional grading.

Literally such a caring professor who just wants everyone to enjoy the class and succeed. If you show up and participate (even in little ways) you will do just fine (obviously also complete the assignments). I loved going to this class because no two classes were ever the same from different discussions to new takes on writing. TAKE THIS CLASS!

I highly recommend taking Prof. Bushnell's class! Not only is he a passionate and caring teacher, but his grading criteria is clear from day one. He is helpful and accessible outside of class, and the material discussed in class is engaging. I learned more from this writing class than any other Writing/English class I've taken.

Professor Bushnell is great! He is always looking to help you and if you go to his office hours he definitely will help you a ton! Participate in class a lot, keep up with the minimal readings he assigns, and hand  in the three papers on time following the rubric and you'll be fine. He is my fave english teacher ever and is super fair! Love him!

analysis.name: Elizabeth Bucar
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sends email to class saying it is "dangerous" to post reviews here. beware.

Participation is really important, so you should talk every class. Easy to pass but hard to do well. Interesting but only learn a topic from one specific author so you don't learn as much as you could. And don't yawn...

Prof. Bucar is excellent at teaching this class. This class is an easy A, just do your work on time. Theres lots of discussion posts and essays but could all be completed within a reasonable amount of time. I highly recommend this class if you are taking for credit or NUpath. Put effort into this class, work should only take about 1-2 hours weekly!

Took her 'Selling Spirituality' class in Fall 2024 and it was great. flipped classroom, so did all the readings at home and the discussion and work in class. LOTS OF READING. but as long as you submit your notes and actually do the readings and go to class, and don't use ChatGPT for any assignments, you will do fine. Easy A. Would take again.
topic is interesting but it is strictly a reading analysis class. would've liked to hear her opinions. guest lecturer was the best part.

analysis.name: Lynn Burke
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I don't appreciate how much work must be done for a ONE-CREDIT CLASS, and why her TA grades part of some assignments but she grades others. The feedback from both is subjective, so it's difficult to know whose advice to follow. She often asks painfully obvious questions and makes it clear that she knows little about the architecture field.

She's really helpful but she goes over the same things a lot. One time we spent 2 lessons learning how to use in design when we were already taught it. tbh I think she just needs better coordination with studio class teachers.
Lynn is amazing. She coordinates every Architecture Co-op student, and still makes time to teach a class and visit with employers. If you want to do well at Northeastern, Lynn is the person to know!
Lynn was an amazing co-op class teacher.  The exercises she used to get us ready for co-op were very helpful. Lots of fun! but make sure you show up on time
Lynn gets you ready for co-op and everything she says will help in future. Pay attention because she notices everything you do.

analysis.name: Alex Budnitz
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very good critiques, lots of iteration and work but for the better. Very funny and smart guy. If you take his crits seriously there is no doubt you will improve as a designer. He forces you to think abstractly and on more than one iteration at once, many students find this difficult.

During a critique, I was told my design ‘looks like pad/tampon packaging.' Basic proof of his mediocre background, lack of true knowledge, expertise in the field and of course teaching etiquette. He dictates students to boost his ego. It's sad Northeastern doesn't evaluate professors on merit.

Professor gives no structures to his classes, does not know how to read rooms, made ignorant transphobic remarks in class, did not give helpful feedback, does not respond to emails. He gave helpful career and portfolio guidance, but is heavily graphic design focused. Would not recommend this course

You have to be very good with time management by yourself. All crit based, but he doesn't give good advice. Doesn't really enforce participation, my class was very small and people didn't really talk so i didn't get that much out of it. SO MUCH WORK. He is a fun guy but grade is determined mainly by how much he likes you.

Prof teaches a very loose curriculum and our class had 3 main projects/deliverables. We'd often have a ton of work due with quite vague guidelines (purposefully so, to not hinder creativity as he said it). My class had a lot of people who didn't speak and he was ok with that, which was unfortunate. Unusual experience overall, not one I'd redo.

analysis.name: Byron Wallace
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Taking DS 2000 with Byron was a great experience. He showed beginners like me that you can do many things with python. In class sessions were helpful for homework and quizzes. Truly became on of my favorite professors at Northeastern.

Honestly can't complain. Not his fault that the homework gets annoying at times, it's just the way the class is set up. Knows what he's doing, is happy to help and answer questions, and preps you well for the exams. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll fall behind pretty quickly if you skip (because you work in Racket...). Would recommend.

I was an intern with Dr. Wallace (Byron, as he prefers). He got some really cool insights into the project at hand which made an otherwise obscure topic quite easy to follow. He even replies on weekends if it's urgent and is easily accessible on slack as well as in-person. So easy-going plus enthusiastic plus insightful which is amazing!

He is more well-suited for conducting research instead of instructions. The math algorithms in this course are kind of PhD-level, but he cannot interpret them in an easily understandable way. The examples he uses are complex, hard to follow if you are not experienced in that area. If you are a math genius, take this course!

Byron is a lovable and cheerful professor. Yes, call him Byron and not professor as that's how he prefers it. I actually took him last semester but I wanted to make sure people know he's a good person. The class is kind of tough, especially for new people to CS, so be sure to ask questions and stay ahead of work. Good luck.

analysis.name: Kal Bugrara
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is very short tempered.Being a Program director he controls all other profs of the department. He takes the application engineering class in which the students are supposed to learn swing but in the class he will not teach a single word about swings.Its all self study .If you are planning to take IS be careful he is very arrogant ,gives low grad

I mostly had very good experience with professors except Prof Bugrara.   As a program director he controls other professors in his program and plays politics.  Northeastern University, please hire a better program director since you charge us a lot.
Rude and worst man in person. If you take any class from his department he will dictate other professor to give lower grade.
never take the class from this professor unless its mandatory. Dont expect any grades and morethan that dont expect that u will learn something.

Nice guy... Other than that terrible. He doesn't have a bad stile, the problem is that he teach useless stuff. He needs an urgent update in knowledge and get better TAs (who are usually useless) In general a bad experience in everything class-related

analysis.name: Ki-Young Byun
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You can't just rely on your lecture notes. She is very unclear with her teaching, and going to her office hours and asking questions is useless because her answer most of the time is, "You just gotta know" or she'll give you a page number. She makes it hard to establish a student-teacher relationship. She's always rushy in class and office hours.

Terrible.  Lecture is useless as she usually doesn't know what she is talking about.  Gives practice exams that are usually wrong.  Also, make sure you check your returned exams because she usually makes mistakes while correcting or uses the wrong answers.  Avoid at all costs.  She thinks a class avg below 50 is decent and laughed about it in class

Worst teacher ever.  She has no clue how to teach and does not know what she is talking about in lecture.  She puts material on exams that was not covered in class or the text.  Going to class is pretty much useless as all learning is done through the text.  Gives practice exams but most of the questions on them are incorrectly answered on the key.

During the semester, 2 kids (or the same kid twice) got a question right on the blackboard. Both times resulted in the whole class applauding. I understand Orgo isn't supposed to be easy but unfortunately her lectures make things worse which is frustrating. You'd think that her tests would somehow be related to her lectures but they're far from it

Definitely not a good teacher. If youre looking to be taught organic chemistry, don't take Byun. Everyday I question how she managed to get a PhD in Chemistry, because she has the hardest time answering the simplest questions and frequently gets confused by her notes. Its like she doesn't understand what she's doing. Reading the book is necessary.

analysis.name: Rebecca Carrier
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: nicest professor I've had. This class wasn't hard to get a good grade in, but it was difficult to actually learn/understand the material. She sometimes got confused by her notes during her lectures and then assigned homework that she didn't know how to do. Let us correct quizzes and get extensions when needed.

The nicest prof. I've ever had. Her lectures are pretty clear and the homework prepares you well for tests. Only con was that she was extremely disorganized, but she is a very sweet person and understanding with extensions, which made up for it. Allowed test corrections for half credit, which I know helped a lot of people.

Prof. Carrier is amazing. Her lectures and homework prepare you perfectly for the four quizzes she gives for the semester (no tests/final). She cares deeply about her students and is definitely one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern (especially in the cheme department).

analysis.name: Carolyn Sirois
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's honestly a very sweet and caring person. She gives a lot of great feedback, and her class actually taught me a lot. She takes forever to grade, but I feel like if you converse with her a lot, she will give you a better grade on the essays. It's kind of content-heavy, though, and there are a lot of field trips.

She is very chill and she makes you go outside a lot on fieldtrips and outside of class time for the projects but overall, the projects aren't bad, homework wasn't bad, classes can be boring, you won't know your grade until the end.
She would be a better teacher is she would not go on talking about senseless things.

Although she ramble senselessly and the only improvement you find in your writing is from just having to write over and over again, this course is incredibly easy. As long as you show up, show you put in effort, participate in class, and organize your portfolio you will get an A.

She is very unclear when giving out assigning. It's hard to understand what is she asking for her assignments. Make your essays sound good and you will do well on her class. That's what i found out while taking her class, its how you say it and not what you're saying.

analysis.name: Jennifer  Cassano
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Such a sweet person; she does the best job possible at condensing a dizzying amount of content into one class. Her lecture slides are clear and she provides plenty of online resources in Canvas. Two tests and the final make up the majority of the grade in her class, with a few comparatively small, low-stress assignments/extra credit opportunities.

Prof. Cassano is very nice but you will need to put in effort and work hard to pass this class. There are only two midterms and a final exam that determine your grade. She only gives five homework assignments, which are not even about the chem hw . This class covers two semesters worth of material in one semester.Slides are easy to understand.

Probably one of the best teachers I've had. Lectures and slides are so clear and in-depth. Both walk you through examples step by step. Made accelerated gen chem genuinely enjoyable and somewhat easy. She posts all her slides, resources, practice problems, and textbook (for free) and her Canvas is super organized. Wish she were at Boston campus.

Course was hard but she grades very easily. You can tell that she would much rather be doing cosmetic science and not gen chem.. Very sweet person, not the strongest teacher, she mainly just reads off of the slides and if they're difficult to follow you're cooked.

The course in general was long, but she has lecture heavy slides everyday. Make sure you are VERY familiar with each days content as it goes quick and she does not slow down. Her practice exams are very different from her actual exams. Nice person.

analysis.name: Carlene Hempel
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Don't take this class if you are an athlete.

Hempel was tough in all the right ways. She gives constructive feedback and encourages asking questions with constructive responses. Most of which were explained through an example. Her class was not a cake walk by any means but she truly cares for her students. You need to put forth a lot of effort but she made it enjoyable.

Carlene is an extremely caring teacher who values making close connections with her students. This being said, the class is very fast paced and once you get behind it's impossible to catch up unless you devote all of your time to it. I don't recommend taking the class with other writing heavy classes but if you want great feedback she is perfect.

One of the hardest classes I've ever taken. An intro class but she said, "I teach it like my graduate class." She pushes you to be better, but didn't teach core concepts. You can tell she cares so much, and she wants a close-knit community, but I just always felt stressed. She's very easy to contact though, and will work with you if you need help.

Be prepared to treat journalism like your profession, even as a first-year student. Carlene is super caring and wants her students to succeed but her expectations were unlike anything I've experienced before. Only would recommend for students who are absolutely certain they want to pursue the field of journalism in their future.

analysis.name: Cecelia Musselman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loved Dr. Musselman! She is more than willing to take you under her wing if you show interest. Her essays and projects are made to pull you out of your comfort zone while still being simple. Grading is confusing and vague at times so be sure to ask questions! If you follow her guidelines and listen to her feedback you will do well. Super sweet!
Nice lady and passionate about her work. The history of english course is difficult to grasp, but she is a very kind and fair grader.

Is all about the busy work.  Get on her good side by participating in class and asking her opinion about your papers.  Paper guidelines are very unclear,  I don't think she even understood them.  The worst english teacher I have ever had.

Great Professor. Dr. Musselman will make you appreciate writing and you will enjoy writing about 3 essays and 1 video project/graphic novel. With enough effort and re-writes, you will be able to receive a good grade.

Prof. Musselman is the best writing professor I've had (I am a biochemistry major).  She is very straightforward with what she looks for when grading, provides direct answers and helpful feedback when inquiries are made, well informed, and very approachable.  I highly recommend taking her middler year writing class if you are a science major.

analysis.name: Tamer Cetin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cetin is truly one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. He is super smart, relaxed and encourages participation that really helps us learn. I came into class liking Micro Economics, but three months in and I love that stuff. Definitely recommend!

Teaches from PowerPoints, hard to get much out of them. Tests are easy, based off the 1-2 hw assignments (MC and a few short answers) per unit, and the recitation class right before the test. Super chill, doesn't care if you come to class, very nice guy. Super accessible by email/office hours, v understanding. From Turkey, so his English is ehh.

He's so great and nice! His lecture is relaxing, and he explains everything clearly. He always asks us if we follow him and give a lot of actual examples to help us understand. One more thing here, people complain about his accent a lot. I don't think it 's a problem. English is not my first langue, and I can't understand what he says.
Tamer is the GOAT of Econ. I would like nothing more than to kick back and smoke with him. Chill guy, great flow, class isn't too hard.
You can't really understand him, but all in all not a horrible guy and pretty easy course.

analysis.name: Mehmet Ceyhan
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: this guy has no idea about anything in the subject. he copies the stuff he teaches from other books. he is sooo bad, if you want to understand try to avoid him.

Had him for Digital Simulation.  One of the useless professors I've ever had.  I'm still not sure what I even learned from that class.  Very unclear, and not an easy class.  Nice guy, pretty awful teacher for this subject.
The guy is sooooo bad. he has no idea about the subject and he doesn't know how to teach or anything. avoid him because you will not learn anything and you will spend money for nothing.
Easily the worst teacher i've ever had to deal with. nice enough guy, means well, but NOT knowledgeable in area of study. always blames the TA, is very unprofessional, and CANNOT TEACH.
I don't know how northeastern university hired him as a teacher. The guy has know idea about the subject and has know idea about anything in IE.

analysis.name: David Choffnes
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Choffnes is an expert lecturer with deep knowledge of the material. However, the course workload is extremely high for an intro class. The syllabus is very ambitious, covering a vast amount of content that can be difficult to balance with other courses. It is a highly educational experience, but expect a very rigorous pace and grading.

Prof David is very passionate about Networking, the second half of his lectures are gold mines and will make you love networking, he gave some opportunity for extra credits and he is very accommodating, but project 3/4 needs infrastructure help from college, I really loved his classes, although i messed my finals still ended in decent grades

Class isn't too bad if you are willing to put in the work. Start the group projects early because they count for the majority of the grade. You get a notesheet for the exams which is very helpful. Don't skip lecture, he crams 2 lectures worth of info into each powerpoint. Textbook is not required but I found it very helpful (free online).

David is a nice guy! He knows a lot in his field and is always enthusiastic in class. As long as you fulfill the requirement (code run and get the result) you get whole grade. However the extra credit is challenging. Each assignment takes 1-2 days to finish(3-4 day if you do not familiar with tools) therefore the load is fair.
This is one of the hardest classes I've ever taken, but I did learned a lot about networks. Projects are well designed, exams are quite challenging. Prof. Choffnes is a great lecturer.

analysis.name: Carla Staton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Staton is great at teaching, however grading takes too long(we still don't have our third exams or workshops back after the final). The final was hard and workshops don't resemble tests so our averages were low. It's her first time teaching it, her lectures had a lot of depth. I just wish there was practice that resembled test like questions.

She taught in a way that was easy to understand. She provided many resources to help like test corrections.She falls behind grading and it's really frustrating to have to wait. It would be nice if she communicated when things were taking her longer, she would promise us grades back by a date and then give them back 12 days later.

I loved taking Organic II with Professor Staton. The class is difficult, but with 50% test corrections back on the three midterm exams it's more than fair. She is readily accessible outside of class and genuinely seems to care about her students and the course itself. I definitely recommend for Orgo II.

The negative reviews are uncalled for and just plain rude. Professor Staton is easily one of the best professors at NEU. She is an incredibly smart woman and cares a lot about her students. This class is difficult, but remember she is teaching a very difficult subject. If you're planning on taking Orgo 1 or 2, take it with Staton, she is great.

Really engaging lecturer and cool grading policies (50% corrections on exams). However, her tests are just insanely difficult. The practice exams are not similar at all to the real thing, making it hard to study. She has very little leniency for personal circumstances but is always willing to meet with you. Would've taken Orgo 2 with her if I could

analysis.name: Vishal chawla
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great professor, perfect balance of learning and grading. I got lots of opportunities to practice what I learned with modern tech stacks, fair grading standards. I learned systematically about full stack web development with essential skills for nowadays SDE, I got interviews after took this course.

Everything changes in 2025, it is the most horrible and hard course I‘ve taken. You need 6-8hours for weekly assignment, midterm and quizes' mean are always lower than 70%. What makes it better? in final week, here is a project and final exam waiting for you. Class attending is required, but here is no credits for it.

Course was a letdown. The midterm was packed with way too many MCQs, impossible to finish in time. The TA's grading is super harsh. Attendance is mandatory, so you have to show up even though lectures don't help much with the exams. If you care about your GPA, time, or tuition, I'd strongly recommend avoiding this class.

He just reads the PPT and shows no enthusiasm in classes. There is no difference if you just learn it yourself on Youtube. 
He used to give easy grades to students but NOW everything just changed. His Quizs and Exams become difficult and hard to achieve grades.

I thoroughly enjoyed my time in the course as it provided ample opportunities for me to enhance my knowledge base. The class activities were instrumental in laying a strong foundation for me. The professor's provision of supplementary sources and articles served as invaluable resources for deepening my understanding of the subject matter.

analysis.name: Christopher Miller
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I mean Miller is definitely a great professor, he provides lots of assistance for his students. The information he provides in his PowerPoint is clear and easy for students to understand the different key concepts in the course.  Easy A in the exam if you finish all or most of the exercises he provided in the canvas.

Professor Miller was an all-around great professor. His lectures were well structured, he provided in-class time to go over study guides and challenging concepts which would be covered on the exam, and works hard to give his students a fundamental understanding of the course material. He's also just a personable guy!

Professor Miller is the best accounting professor I've had at NEU. I took Cost Accounting and Financial Statement Analysis with him, and he's been a great mentor ever since. He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed academically and professionally. Highly recommend his classes if you want to really understand accounting.

Best business professor I've had. His tests are pretty much identical to the review material. Extremely friendly and outgoing. Case Studies are pretty much just graded on completion. The only problem is that the HWs can get a bit long and tedious. But other than that it is a low-stress class.

Professor Miller is one of my favorite professors at Northeastern. He's really funny which helps make accounting less boring. The tests can be pretty hard but he gives tons of practice problems that help a lot. When starting a new unit, he has a "slides day" where he goes over the content, and then a "problem day" where we do practice problems.

analysis.name: Alessandra Ciucci
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt
